audit_notes: Slip: Philip/ Lauga-Stone for streamwise ridges, L = 20 um, gas fraction 0.85: b_par = (L/pi) ln(sec(pi*0.85/2)) = 6.37 um * ln(4.28) = 9.3 um, b_perp ~ 4.6 um; net virtual-origin shift ~ b_par - 0.6 b_perp = 6.5 um, so the proposed 5 um net value is conservative. With 70% coverage: 3.5 um -> expected gain 3.5/98.5 = 3.6%. b+ = 0.93. Gas supply: H2 at 0.5 A/m2 = j/(2F) = 2.6e-6 mol/(s m2) = 6.3e-8 m3/(s m2) at 1 bar; plastron volume ~5e-6 m3/m2 -> refill ~80 s (at 10 m depth ~160 s). Energy: 1.5 W/m2 -> 15 kW for 1e4 m2 (0.15% of 10 MW propulsion). CRITICAL side effect (not modelled): the counter-electrode reaction in seawater at 0.5 A/m2 * 1e4 m2 = 5000 A is chlorine/hypochlorite evolution: 5000/(2*96485)*70.9 g/mol = 1.8 g/s = ~160 kg active chlorine per day at full duty (~16 kg/day at 10% duty). Typical ICCP currents on a coated hull are only 10-30 mA/m2 (100-300 A), so this is 20-50x more anodic product, i.e. an electrochemical biocide in practice. Cathodic current density 0.5 A/m2 also precipitates calcareous deposits (CaCO3, Mg(OH)2) at pH > 9.5 on the cathode mesh, which will clog the ridges over months. Laplace breakthrough ~2*0.072*0.5/17e-6 = 4.2 kPa (0.4 m head): the plastron is depth-limited without continuous regeneration. Structural: ridges fine under 50 Pa shear; the buried conductive mesh must not contact the steel (galvanic/ hydrogen embrittlement risk). Physically consistent, so audit passes, but the non-toxic requirement is at risk. Baseline: smooth FR hull (slip 0).

performance_gain.label: Skin-friction reduction vs clean FR hull

hard_constraints: anodic chlorine production must stay below regulatory discharge limits

baseline_description: Clean smooth silicone foul-release hull (no plastron)
